items.q: Donald Trump has threatened to wage a full-fledged economic war on Iran. Many say the economic threat is aimed at making up for the failure of the war, in the military domain, that the U.S. and Israel waged against Iran. What’s your take on that?
items.a: Sanctions and pressure tactics are not the solution. China calls on parties to act responsibly and stick to the political and diplomatic approach.

items.q: A cross-party group of Japanese lawmakers will reportedly visit China next week, noting that the status quo of Japan-China relations is in no one’s interest. They hope to play a role in improving the bilateral ties. What’s your comment?
items.a: We notice that some visionary people from both Japan’s ruling and opposition parties are deeply concerned over the current state of China-Japan relations and wish to make an effort to restore the relations to the right track. We call on those running the government of Japan to take these concerns seriously, abide by the four political documents, and create the conditions necessary for normal exchanges between China and Japan with concrete actions.

items.q: Yesterday the DPRK fired over ten ballistic missiles toward waters to its east. This marks its 12th launch this year and the largest-scale launch in three years. Does China have any comment?
items.a: We noted the reports and do not have any new comment.

items.q: Iran has endured years of sanctions imposed by the U.S. The Islamic Republic has either managed to bypass or find alternatives. And now it is said that Trump has no tangible card to enforce what he claims as “toughest sanctions.” What’s your viewpoint?
items.a: China believes that military means, sanctions and pressure tactics are not the solution. On the contrary, they will only lead to escalation that serves no one’s interests. We call for efforts to solve disputes through dialogue and negotiation.

items.a: China has released information on Foreign Minister Wang Yi’s visit to Finland. China’s position on the Ukraine crisis and stance on nuclear-related issues are consistent and clear. We remain committed to promoting peace talks and a political settlement of the crisis.

items.a: We noted relevant reports. items.q: Yesterday, during his meeting with President Xi in Bishkek, President Putin said that Russia is ready to make the visa-free regime permanent if the Chinese side considers this possible and useful. What is the foreign ministry’s comment on this?
items.a: Mutual visa exemption speaks to the high-level strategic mutual trust between China and Russia and helps further facilitate cross-border travel, deepen the friendship between our two peoples, and promote exchanges and cooperation in various fields.

items.a: To provide emergency assistance to Nepal’s disaster-hit areas and carry out international rescue and relief cooperation is an important political decision of China and embodies our friendship with Nepal. The second batch of relief supplies provided by China to Nepal is expected to be sent later today. items.a: We have released information on President Xi Jinping’s participation in the SCO Bishkek summit, during which he had cordial exchanges with leaders of various countries.

items.a: Dialogue and negotiation is the only viable way out of the Ukraine crisis. We urge the parties concerned to remain calm and exercise restraint, jointly work toward early deescalation and accumulate conditions for the political settlement of the crisis.

items.a: As an important member of the G20, China places high emphasis on the organization’s role as the premier forum for international economic cooperation. items.a: On September 1, President Xi Jinping attended the 26th meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization and delivered important remarks titled “Toward Higher Quality Development of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization.” President Xi pointed out that over the past 25 years, the SCO has traveled an extraordinary journey. Its biggest achievement is that it has steadily grown into a new type of regional cooperation organization with the largest land area and population and enormous development potential.

items.a: China has more than once made clear its position on the test launch. Palau has repeatedly raised this issue in an ill-intentioned attempt to hijack the position of other member states of the Pacific Islands Forum. It will not have its way. China is committed to peaceful development and a national defense policy that is defensive in nature. We never engage in military expansion. China stands ready to work with South Pacific countries to contribute to peace, stability, development and prosperity of the South Pacific region.

We are making active and sound efforts towards the carbon peak and neutrality goals and expected to make the world’s biggest cut in carbon emission intensity. items.a: China has on many occasions made clear its position on the test launch. China is committed to peaceful development and a national defense policy that is defensive in nature. items.a: On the specifics you mentioned, I have no information to share. China and the U.S. need to jointly deliver on the important common understandings between the two presidents, and maintain the steady growth momentum of China-U.S. economic and trade ties.

items.a: I just shared information on the relevant question. For more specifics, I’d refer you to competent authorities.

items.a: China stays committed to the principle of non-interference in other countries’ internal affairs, and advocates that all countries’ right to follow development path that suits the national conditions should be respected. items.a: China handles cases involving illegal or criminal activities by foreign nationals on Chinese soil in accordance with the law and ensures that their lawful rights are fully protected. I’d refer you to Chinese competent authorities for more information.

items.a: Regional elections in Germany are its domestic affair. China will not comment on that. China’s position on developing its relations with Germany is consistent.

items.q: The United States and China will hold talks on AI safety risks in coming weeks. This is according to a recent report by Reuters. Can the foreign ministry confirm these talks? They will reportedly take place in mid-September. What are Chinese expectations for these discussions?
items.a: China and the U.S. maintain communication on AI.

items.q: Venezuela says its agreements with China will be respected and Chinese joint ventures will continue operating. Has Caracas given Beijing specific assurances that Chinese oil interests will not be affected by the new U.S.-Venezuela agreement?
items.a: Cooperation between China and Venezuela is under the protection of international law and laws of both countries. It has nothing to do with any third party and should not be disrupted by any third party. China’s lawful rights and interests in Venezuela must be protected.

For certain countries like Palau, having Taiwan as a “diplomatic ally” is not about delivering for the country and the people, but to line the pockets of the very few people who profit from it.

items.q: We spoke to the Philippines’ defense secretary earlier today and he said China could use recently scaled-down U.S.-South Korean military exercises as an opportunity to assert itself in the Indo-Pacific region. Do you have anything to say to that comment?
items.a: China is always committed to maintaining peace and stability in the Asia Pacific, and does not engage in major-country confrontation. We hope other regional countries will also play a positive role for peace and stability in the region.

items.a: China sets great store by BRICS cooperation. We support India in hosting a successful BRICS summit this year. For your specific questions, I don’t have more information to offer at the moment.
